newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan August bad-cheque ratio stable at 0.59 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan August bad-cheque ratio stable at 0.59 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's bad-cheque ratio was at 0.59 percent in August, the same as in July but down from 0.60 percent in June, the central bank said on Monday.
Bad cheques totalled 100,182, or 0.59 percent of the total in August, with a value of T$19.3 billion, or 0.42 percent of the value of all cheques written, the bank said in a statement.
The monthly bad-cheque ratio hit a 10-year high of 0.80 percent in October 1995, it said.
In annual terms, 1995's 0.67 percent was also the highest in 10 years. In 1985, the ratio hit 0.75 percent.

The bank attributed the rising number of bad cheques in 1995 to the slow economy and the falling property and stock markets. But in recent months, the bad-cheque problems have eased gradually, it said.
